'''''Cryptogramma crispa''''', the '''parsley fern''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is an [[Arctic–alpine]] species of [[fern]] native to Europe and parts of Asia. It produces separate sterile and fertile fronds, up to {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall, and is a [[pioneer species]] on acidic [[scree]]s.

==Description==
The [[frond]]s of ''C. crispa'' are {{convert|30|cm}} long and appear in two distinct forms. Sterile leaves are 2–3-[[:wikt:pinnate|pinnate]] with the pinnules {{convert|5|-|10|mm|1|abbr=on}} long by  {{convert|3|-|7|mm|1|abbr=on}} wide, while fertile leaves are 3–4-pinnate, and with narrower pinnules.<ref>{{cite book |author=[[Clive A. Stace]] |title=New Flora of the British Isles |edition=3rd |year=2010 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-70772-5 |chapter=''Cryptogramma'' R. Br. – Parsley Fern |page=19}}</ref> The fertile leaves have [[sorus|sori]] scattered along the veins, each with a strongly enrolled false [[indusium]]. The [[sporangium|sporangia]] are yellow and mature around [[midsummer]].<ref name="Hardy"/>

==Distribution and ecology==
''Cryptogramma crispa'' grows among acidic rocks, often in areas where snow lies until late in the year. It is a [[pioneer species]] on stable [[scree|scree slopes]] and also occurs on [[cliff]]s and [[dry stone|dry stone walls]].<ref>{{cite book |title=New Atlas of the British and Irish Flora: An Atlas of the Vascular Plants of Britain, Ireland, The Isle of Man and the Channel Islands |editor=C. D. Preston, D. A. Pearman & T. D. Dines |author=T. D. Dines |chapter=Parsley Fern ''Cryptogramma crispa'' (L.) R.Br. ex Hook. |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |year=2002 |url=https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.v3z |isbn=978-0-19-851067-3}}</ref>

In Europe and western Asia, ''C. crispa'' has an [[Arctic–alpine]] distribution,<ref name="Page">{{cite book |author=Christopher Nigel Page |year=1997 |title=The ferns of Britain and Ireland |edition=2nd |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-58658-0 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Toa-KZD48n0C&pg=PA148 |chapter=''Cryptogramma crispa'' (L.) Hook. |pages=148–151}}</ref> growing in the mountains of [[Central Europe|Central]] and [[Southern Europe]], as well as in the north of the continent, including [[Scandinavia]] and higher ground in the [[British Isles]].<ref>{{cite book |editor=[[Jaakko Jalas|J. Jalas]] & J. Suominen |year=1972 |title=Atlas Florae Europaeae. Distribution of Vascular Plants in Europe. 1. Pteridophyta (Psilotaceae to Azollaceae) |publisher=The Committee for Mapping the Flora of Europe & Societas Biologica Fennica Vanamo |location=Helsinki |pages=121 pp}}</ref> In [[Ireland]], it is rare and concentrated in the east of the country, leading Praeger to conjecture that the Irish examples are recent colonists from [[Great Britain]], arriving as airborne spores.<ref name="Godwin">{{cite book |author=[[Harry Godwin|Sir Harry Godwin]] |year=1956 |title=The history of the British flora: a factual basis for Phytogeography |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |url=https://archive.org/details/historyofbritish0000godw |url-access=registration|chapter=Adiantaceae |page=[https://archive.org/details/historyofbritish0000godw/page/92 92]}}</ref> It is a rare, amber-listed plant of moderate conservation concern in the [[Isle of Man]] where it is a protected species listed on Schedule 7 of the Wildlife Act 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wildlife Act 1990 |url=https://legislation.gov.im/cms/images/LEGISLATION/PRINCIPAL/1990/1990-0002/1990-0002_2.pdf |website=legislation.gov.im}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Plants of Conservation Concern Isle of Man 2022 | Manx Wildlife Trust | url=https://www.mwt.im/PoCCIoM }}</ref>

The species also occurs in eastern Asia in Japan, Korea, and on the Russian island of Sakhalin.<ref name="POWO">{{cite web |title=''Cryptogramma crispa'' (L.) R.Br. |website=Plants of the World Online |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:17070940-1 |access-date=2026-06-21}}</ref> 

Similar plants in western [[North America]] which were formerly sometimes considered [[variety (botany)|varieties]] or [[subspecies]] of ''C. crispa'',<ref>{{cite book |author=[[Eric Hultén]] |title=Flora of Alaska and neighboring territories: a manual of the vascular plants |year=1968 |publisher=[[Stanford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-8047-0643-8 |url=https://archive.org/details/floraofalaskanei0000hult |url-access=registration |chapter=''Cryptogramma'' R. Br. |pages=[https://archive.org/details/floraofalaskanei0000hult/page/44 44]–45}}</ref> are now usually considered separate species, ''[[Cryptogramma acrostichoides]]'',<ref>{{cite web |title=''Cryptogramma acrostichoides'' R.Br. |website=Plants of the World Online |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:1006906-2 |access-date=2026-06-21}}</ref> and ''[[Cryptogramma sitchensis]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Cryptogramma sitchensis'' (Rupr.) T.Moore |website=Plants of the World Online |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:17071030-1 |access-date=2026-06-21}}</ref>

[[Spore]]s attributable to ''C. crispa'' have been discovered in deposits in [[Snowdonia]] from the [[last glacial period]], as well as from more low-lying sites in [[Cheshire]].<ref name="Godwin"/>

==Taxonomic history==
The parsley fern appeared in [[Carl Linnaeus]]' 1753 work ''[[Species Plantarum]]'', the starting point for [[botanical nomenclature]], under the name ''Osmunda crispa''. The [[specific name (botany)|specific epithet]] ''crispa'' means finely waved or curled.<ref name="Hardy">{{cite web |url=http://hardyfernlibrary.com/ferns/listSpecies.cfm?Auto=165 |title=''Cryptogramma crispa'' (L.) R. Br. ex Richardson |publisher=Hardy Fern Library |accessdate=20 July 2010}}</ref> It is placed in the family [[Pteridaceae]], part of the order [[Polypodiales]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Maarten J. M. Christenhusz, Xian-Chun Zhang & Harald Schneider |year=2011 |title=A linear sequence of extant families and genera of lycophytes and ferns |journal=[[Phytotaxa]] |volume=19 |issue=1 |pages=7–54 |doi=10.11646/phytotaxa.19.1.2 |bibcode=2011Phytx..19....7C |url=http://www.mapress.com/phytotaxa/content/2011/f/pt00019p054.pdf }}</ref>
